analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of .github/workflows/release-provider.yml (550–1496) against the complete changed-range map and bounded patch. The visible changes move release staging/publication Linux jobs from Blacksmith to ubuntu-24.04 (base 1210, 1319) and add a 90-minute signing-job timeout (head 343 in patch); other runner changes at 135/304 need their surrounding source examined in integration. No concrete regression is established here.
Relevant contracts are release-key custody (A-005), binary registry and exact artifact qualification (A-011/A-017, T-054), runtime secrecy claims (T-056), and availability (A-018). The supplied surrounding workflow retains signing-key removal before executing signed products (base 715–718), entitlement validation (779–782), final artifact hashes (994–1020), publication identity retention (1147–1195), digest/run-bound artifact downloads (1302–1304, 1423–1425), stage-before-register dependencies (1317–1318), and serialized publication (1324–1326). These controls are not changed by the supplied range map. Provider encryption, cache isolation (T-041), billing, and privileged local helpers have no changed behavior in this scope.
Integration should examine resolve-env/qualification context at 135/304 and reconcile any explicit runner-custody requirements with the new Linux runner selection; macOS signed-artifact work remains on Blacksmith. The publication/download scripts are referenced, not supplied, so their implementation is not verified here. The runner-label change alone does not prove weaker isolation or credential exposure, and the timeout alone does not establish unsafe cleanup or a publication bypass.
